title: Tenant-aware adaptive fan-in prioritizer for live usage events
creator: Morgan Lee
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a tenant-aware adaptive fan-in prioritizer for the console usage event stream so we can (1) reduce P99 processing latency for high-SLA tenants during bursts, (2) prevent noisy tenants from starving others, and (3) provide predictable backpressure behavior that integrates with our existing queueing layer. This is part of the Console Analytics Revamp (project) and complements the per-tenant multiplexing work (ENG-67211).

Goals and success metrics:
- Reduce p99 end-to-end processing latency for top-10 tenants by >= 30% in burst scenarios.
- Keep prioritized-event drop rate < 0.1% under 2x baseline traffic.
- No regression in overall throughput; cost delta < 8% for steady-state traffic.

Proposed design (high level):
- Introduce a lightweight prioritizer node that sits between the ingestion consumer (Kafka/stream consumer) and the enrichment/worker pool.
- Maintain per-tenant priority buckets: SLA-high, SLA-medium, SLA-low, plus a dynamic "hotkey" bucket for tenants exhibiting sudden burst delta.
- Admission control algorithm: token-bucket per-bucket with cross-bucket loaning underutilization; hotkey detection via sketch-based delta counters (count-min) to avoid full state scans.
- Processing policy: serve from high->hotkey->medium->low; if high bucket saturates, preempt medium/low up to a configured preemption ratio.
- Backpressure integration: expose lease tokens back to consumer to slow Kafka commits when in sustained saturation; fall back to FIFO when feature-flag disabled.
- Telemetry: per-tenant queue depth, bucket occupancy, preemption events, token leaks, p50/p95/p99 latencies. Set up new Grafana panel group and alerts.

Trade-offs considered:
- Exact per-tenant counters vs. sketch approximations: chose Count-Min sketch for hotkey detection to bound memory at cost of occasional false positives; acceptable because false positive only increments hotkey promotion which is reversible.
- Centralized priority controller vs. local (node-level) decisions: chosen hybrid approach — node-local buckets with periodic rebalancing from global coordinator to avoid single-point bottleneck.
- Aggressive preemption improves SLAs for high-tier tenants but can starve low-tier customers; mitigated via preemption ratio config and gradual escalation window.

Implementation plan and milestones:
1) Prototype prioritizer module and local bucket controller (PoC) — 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-17.
2) Integrate sketch-based hotkey detector and expose metrics — 2026-03-18 to 2026-03-22.
3) End-to-end testing on staging with synthetic burst tests and canary wiring for 10 tenants — 2026-03-23 to 2026-03-27.
4) Gradual rollout (feature-flag) + monitor/rollback playbook — target 2026-03-31 for GA behind feature flag.

Test plan and validation:
- Synthetic workload generator that replays tenant traffic traces (stored in S3) at 0.5x/1x/2x/5x baseline.
- Chaos tests: worker-node termination and network partitions to validate safe fallback to FIFO path.
- Performance gating: must pass pre-deploy benchmark suite (p50/p99 targets) and automated canary checks.

Rollout strategy and safety knobs:
- Feature flag gating per-cluster and per-tenant.
- Canary rollout to non-critical tenants first (10 tenants), then escalate to top customers after 48h.
- Automatic rollback if p99 increases > 10% or prioritized-event drop > 0.5% for 10m window.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- What exact tenant SLA tiers will map to SLA-high/medium/low? (Need PM input)
- Retention for sketch state between restarts — do we persist and replay? (Ops preference likely ephemeral, but need confirmation)
- Default preemption ratio and token-bucket sizes per hardware profile.

Artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/Tenant+Fan-In+Prioritizer
- PoC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/8392
- Staging dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abc123/console-ingest-latency?orgId=1

Next steps (owner: Aisha Patel):
- Finalize SLA tier mapping with PM (scheduled meeting 2026-03-12).
- Ship PoC and request initial review from runtime team (PR linked).
- Coordinate with infra to allocate a staging cluster for canary tests.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Morgan Lee: Created initial ticket and uploaded design overview. Marked dependency on ENG-67211 to reuse tenant multiplexing primitives.
2026-03-11 — Aisha Patel: Implemented PoC for local bucket controller; initial simulation shows 28% p99 improvement for top tenants at 2x burst. Added PoC PR link.

2026-03-12 — Tomás Rivera (runtime): Reviewed PoC; requested hybrid coordinator approach instead of pure local to avoid cross-node starvation in multi-partition consumers. Raised concerns about memory for exact counters; recommended Count-Min sketch option.
2026-03-12 — Priya Menon (PM): Confirmed SLA tier mapping session scheduled 2026-03-12. Agreed on conservative default preemption ratio of 0.15 pending customer impact review.
2026-03-13 — Aisha Patel: Updated PoC to use Count-Min sketch and added token-bucket loaning. Running extended replay tests on staging cluster. Next: add Grafana panels and set alert thresholds.
2026-03-13 — Security (note): No immediate secrets or KMS work; secure config review on feature flag path recommended before GA.
